title: Wake-up and extended-window thrombolysis
summary: Wake-up and extended-window IVT require trial-specific imaging and time criteria. Newer tenecteplase trials give different answers for LVO without access to EVT, non-LVO, and planned EVT.
consider: Confirm last known well, symptom discovery and whether selection uses MRI DWI–FLAIR mismatch or perfusion imaging.
TRACE-III (LVO without EVT access) and OPTION (non-LVO) found better 90-day functional outcomes in perfusion-selected Chinese cohorts; both reported more symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage.
TIMELESS (77% received EVT) and TNK-PLUS (planned EVT) did not demonstrate functional benefit from late-window tenecteplase.
Review the complete trial criteria, remaining exclusions, current guidance and EVT plan before generalizing.
caution: These results do not establish routine late-window IVT for every stroke or make MRI mismatch and perfusion selection interchangeable. The 2021 ESO document predates these tenecteplase trials.

title: Medium and distal vessel occlusion
summary: Randomized results differ: DISTAL and ESCAPE-MeVO were neutral, while ORIENTAL-MeVO found more functional independence, with more symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, in selected Chinese patients with moderate-to-severe deficits. The SVIN guideline searched evidence through February 2026, before ORIENTAL-MeVO publication.
consider: Confirm vessel segment, dominance, disabling deficit, imaging and time window; the trial populations are not interchangeable.
Compare ORIENTAL-MeVO’s NIHSS eligibility of at least 6 and 24-hour window with the neutral trials and their procedural risks.
Discuss the complete evidence and remaining reperfusion options with the intervention team.
caution: SVIN did not support routine DMVO EVT and considered selected disabling dominant-M2 treatment reasonable. A newer positive trial does not establish benefit for every M2 or distal lesion; neutral trials do not establish equivalence.

title: Acute retinal ischemia and CRAO
summary: CRAO remains an emergency. In nonarteritic CRAO treated within 4.5 hours, THEIA did not demonstrate improved one-month visual acuity with alteplase versus aspirin and was likely underpowered. TenCRAOS found no significant 30-day vision-recovery benefit with tenecteplase and reported one fatal intracranial hemorrhage.
consider: Confirm the ophthalmologic diagnosis and onset; coordinate urgent stroke and ophthalmology assessment.
Assess the vascular mechanism and whether an arteritic cause is suspected; these trials studied nonarteritic CRAO.
Distinguish improvement in visual acuity in THEIA from the vision-recovery threshold in TenCRAOS, and review safety alongside benefit.
caution: Small neutral trials do not prove equivalence or establish routine IVT benefit. The 2021 AHA statement predates these randomized results; review the current local pathway and systemic vascular risk.

title: Large infarction, swelling and decompression

caution: Reducing intracranial pressure does not itself establish improved long-term function. Late decompression and some posterior-fossa decisions have important evidence gaps.

In OCEANIC-AF it increased stroke/systemic embolism versus apixaban despite less major bleeding. Nerinetide, conditioning and colchicine require trial-specific interpretation.
consider: Identify the mechanism, background therapy and primary endpoint before comparing a new treatment with standard care.
Compare neutral ESCAPE-NEXT/RESIST and colchicine findings with the selected positive SERIC-EVT population; distinguish confirmatory outcomes from subgroup signals.
Check independent replication, safety uncertainty, current guidance and authorization before clinical adoption.
caution: Research results do not establish availability, approval or an individualized treatment recommendation. Avoid treating diverse adjunct drugs or conditioning strategies as a single effective class.

title: Rapid appraisal of a trial or guideline
summary: Use a structured appraisal before converting a study headline into a clinical decision: population, comparison, outcome, uncertainty and applicability.
consider: Is the outcome patient-important, and is the quoted result the prespecified primary analysis?
Compare absolute and relative effects, confidence intervals, missing data and harms.
Check whether subgroup, noninferiority or composite-endpoint claims support the proposed inference.
caution: A neutral superiority trial does not prove equivalence. A source title, evidence level or publication date alone does not establish validity or relevance.

title: ICH expansion and intraventricular extension
summary: Hemostatic treatment and removal of ventricular blood address different problems. TICH-2 and CLEAR III illustrate why less bleeding or lower mortality must be distinguished from improved functional outcome.
consider: Clarify whether the immediate problem is expansion, ventricular obstruction, hydrocephalus or mass effect.
Compare the intervention, anatomy and outcome with the actual trial population.
Discuss neurosurgical and neurocritical-care options, procedural risks and patient-valued outcomes.
caution: Neither trial established improvement in its primary functional endpoint. The studies do not create an automatic hemostatic-drug or intraventricular-lytic protocol.
